annotation.evidence_span: stream identifier field value other than 0x0
annotation.interpretation_a: Any non-zero value in the stream identifier field triggers a PROTOCOL_ERROR.
annotation.interpretation_b: Only values other than 0x0 that are *valid* stream IDs (i.e., not already in use) trigger a PROTOCOL_ERROR. An invalid stream ID might be handled differently.
annotation.justification: The clause states that a PING frame with a stream identifier other than 0x0 MUST cause a connection error. However, it doesn't specify what to do if the non-zero stream ID is already in use for another stream. This creates ambiguity because an implementation could either treat it as a protocol error, or handle it as a stream-level error (or some other error condition).
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether the requirement applies to all non-zero values, or only to valid (unused) stream IDs. The specification does not define how to handle a PING frame with an already-in-use stream ID.
